title: Tests clean up their temp folders, in every repo
why: Oct 22: Degen's Swift tests left temp folders that filled the Mac disk (note from the Degen session).
note: Pattern from Degen (branch temp-dir-leak): one temp root per repo; a <pid>-<UUID> run folder; every helper takes its folder from it; teardown removes it; the first request of a run removes sibling run folders older than a day (crashed runs) and keeps newer ones (parallel runs); a test proves the sweep. claude-settings has no such rule; the nearest home is the janitor (debt windows-temp-sweep, ruled Oct 16, never built: session temp folders, 17 GB on Windows). Rule only; each repo keeps its own helper, no copying code across repos. Both are lanes in batch 3 of briefs/cleanup-goal-2-oct23.md (full text on c37). Ties to the brake: disk filling up is what full guards. claude-settings part landed in #567 (batch-oct23b, Oct 23), checked at claude-settings f463787 (main, Oct 25): the run-folder standard is in agents/test-author.md, and the janitor removes idle session temp folders on Windows (debt windows-temp-sweep built). Each repo's own helper (Degen's TempDirSupport.swift) stays with that repo; not checked here.
ask: See c37 (goal 2), batch 3, lanes test-temp-standard and windows-temp-sweep.
